sub_questions.question: After fixing a typo in an uploaded document, do I need to delete and re-upload it, or will it update on its own?

claims.claim: There is no need to delete and re-upload the document.
claims.guide_evidence: When a document is edited and saved, it is re-processed through these same four stages

claims.claim: An edited and saved document is automatically re-processed through parse, enrich, chunk and re-index.
claims.guide_evidence: When a document is edited and saved, it is re-processed through these same four stages before its chunks are available for retrieval again

claims.claim: The document's chunks become available for retrieval again only after re-processing finishes.
claims.guide_evidence: before its chunks are available for retrieval again

claims.claim: While the document is re-processing, the previous version stays fully searchable, so retrieval keeps working with no gap.
claims.guide_evidence: a newly indexed document is not searchable mid-processing

evaluation.rationale: The answer is right that editing and saving starts automatic re-processing, so there is no need to delete and re-upload. But it says the previous version stays fully searchable with no gap. That contradicts the guide, which says the chunks are not available for retrieval until re-processing finishes. This overconfident claim could lead the customer to edit live documents expecting no retrieval gap.
